newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU postpones final stance on Singapore talks.
newsitem.headline: EU postpones final stance on Singapore talks.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers on Monday put off finalising a common position for a series of key meetings with Asian partners next month, but officials said there was nothing untoward in the delay.

EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels were due to finalise their stance for two key gatherings in Singapore -- one with their counterparts from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the other under the Europe-Asia Meeting (ASEM) umbrella.

But the ministers delayed agreeing a final draft until they had consulted further with Asia. "It is not unusual," said one diplomat. "Often with these meetings we do not rubber stamp our position until we have let the other parties know what it is."
The EU's ties with Asian organisations have gone through some rough patches in recent years -- particularly over relations between former colonial powers and their colonies.

Portugal, for example, has frequently protested through the EU about Indonesian policy in its former colony East Timor. The Netherlands, as Indonesia's former colonial power, also has an interest in this.
More recently, links betweem Asia and Europe have been strained by ASEAN plans to enlarge to take in Burma which the EU frequently criticises for human rights abuses.

The ASEAN meeting on February 13-14 will include new member Vietnam for the first time and, with plans to take in Cambodia, Laos and Burma in the near future, the EU is making sure it does not take the bloc lightly.
The EU has become ASEAN's third biggest trade partner with over 70 billion European currency units (Ecus) ($85 billion) in goods and services changing hands in 1994-95.

The February 15 ASEM meeting -- which takes in ASEAN members Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam with China, Japan and South Korea -- is to focus on establishing an Asia-Europe Foundation to fund cultural exchanges.
